text: The setup guide had six screens. I wasn't sure which step mattered first, so I left it until the next day. Once someone walked me through it, I could finish.
We like the idea, but I need to know who approves the replies before we turn it on. If we can review them first, I'd feel better about a pilot.
I thought the dashboard would show every inquiry instantly. It takes a little while to sync, and nobody explained that. The delay made me think it was broken.
The team already has a morning routine in our old system. Asking them to open another tab means one more thing to remember. A daily digest might fit better.
The short checklist helped. I know what to do first now, but I'm still unsure when to hand a conversation to a person.
We tried the review queue. Seeing the draft before it goes out helps me trust the workflow, although approval takes time when we're busy.
The sync status label makes the delay clear. I don't wonder if it's broken anymore. I'd still like a notification when a record is ready.
I would need to see a real example before recommending it to our teams. The overview sounds promising, but I'm uncertain how it handles unusual requests.
The daily digest fits our routine better than another dashboard. Two team members are using it, though I can't say whether it changed response time yet.
The handoff examples helped us decide when to step in. Our team uses the queue most days now, but we still review edge cases together.
The example library answered some questions. I still want a way to test an unusual request safely before enabling the feature.
We trust the drafts more after reviewing them for a month. The approval queue is still slow on busy days, so we'd like a faster way to handle routine cases.
